session.question: How do thermal pwer plants relate to the environmental issues described in the survey on energy-efficient techniques in sustainable cloud computing?
session.answer:
Thermal power plants are presented as an indirect but important source of the environmental problems motivating sustainable cloud computing. The survey explains that the electricity consumed by data centers and other computing infrastructure is often generated by thermal power plants, which rely mainly on fossil fuels such as coal and oil. (bharany2022asystematicsurvey chunk 1)

Because these fuels are associated with high CO2 emissions and pollution, thermal power plants contribute to global warming, ozone layer depletion, and premature deaths of living beings. In this framing, the environmental impact of cloud computing is not only due to server-side energy use, but also to the upstream power generation mix supplying that energy. (bharany2022asystematicsurvey chunk 1)

Accordingly, the survey positions energy-efficient and green cloud computing techniques as a response to these harms. By reducing electricity demand in cloud data centers, such techniques lower dependence on fossil-fuel-based thermal generation and thereby reduce associated emissions and environmental damage. (bharany2022asystematicsurvey chunk 1)

pqac-d0346d86: The excerpt explains that thermal power plants, which generate much of the energy used by data centers and computing infrastructure, rely mainly on fossil fuels such as coal and oil. This contributes to environmental problems including global warming, ozone layer depletion, and even premature deaths of living beings due to pollution. The paper frames sustainable cloud computing as a response to these issues by reducing energy consumption and CO2 emissions in cloud data centers. It surveys energy-efficient techniques such as VM virtualization and consolidation, power-aware methods, bio-inspired approaches, and thermal management to lower energy use and environmental impact.
From Salil Bharany, Sandeep Sharma, Osamah Ibrahim Khalaf, Ghaida Muttashar Abdulsahib, Abeer S. Al Humaimeedy, Theyazn H. H. Aldhyani, Mashael Maashi, and Hasan Alkahtani. pqac-1f8ea63c: The excerpt discusses cloud computing’s large and growing energy demand, noting that data centres may consume 20% of global electricity and emit up to 5.5% of the world’s carbon emissions by 2025. A significant portion of this energy becomes heat, causing operational issues such as reduced reliability, shorter device life, and increased cooling needs. The paper argues that future cloud systems must be energy-efficient and environmentally sustainable, proposing learning-centric integrated management of resources and workloads to reduce energy consumption and carbon footprint while maintaining service quality. It does not mention thermal power plants directly, but the broader environmental concern is carbon emissions and energy waste.
From Rajkumar Buyya, Shashikant Ilager, and Patricia Arroba. Energy‐efficiency and sustainability in new generation cloud computing: a vision and directions for integrated management of data centre resources and workloads. Software Practice and Experience, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.1002/spe.3248, doi:10.1002/spe.3248.

pqac-85dad99f: The excerpt explains that large energy consumption in data centers contributes to global energy use and carbon emissions, motivating sustainable cloud computing. It focuses on federated cloud computing, where geographically distributed data centers can be leveraged to reduce energy consumption and carbon emissions by choosing where to schedule tasks. The ERLFC framework uses reinforcement learning (Actor-Critic) to assign tasks based on factors like energy consumption, cooling method, waiting time, energy type, emission ratio, and current energy use. It reports reductions in energy saving and emission reduction compared with baseline schedulers, showing how energy-efficient techniques can support environmentally sustainable cloud computing.
From Zhibao Wang, Shuaijun Chen, Lu Bai, Juntao Gao, Jinhua Tao, Raymond R. Bond, and Maurice Mulvenna. Reinforcement learning based task scheduling for environmentally sustainable federated cloud computing. Journal of Cloud Computing Advances Systems and Applications, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.1186/s13677-023-00553-0, doi:10.1186/s13677-023-00553-0.

pqac-e9768f78: The excerpt does not specifically discuss thermal power plants or their environmental problems. It focuses on integrating IoT and cloud computing in power systems to improve sustainability and efficiency, emphasizing Cloud of Things (CoT), data processing, storage, analytics, and resource optimization. The paper argues that these technologies support more sustainable energy systems and efficient power distribution, including renewable energy, distributed generation, electric vehicles, and grid-to-vehicle technologies. It links cloud-based approaches to better resource utilization, reliability, and reduced energy waste in power infrastructure, but it does not mention emissions, pollution, or other thermal power plant impacts directly.
From R. Arul, S. Dhivya, Mohit Bajaj, Issam Damaj, Rajkumar Singh Rathore, Arvind R. Singh, Vojtěch Blažek, and Lukáš Prokop. session.formatted_answer:
Question: How do thermal pwer plants relate to the environmental issues described in the survey on energy-efficient techniques in sustainable cloud computing?

Thermal power plants are presented as an indirect but important source of the environmental problems motivating sustainable cloud computing. The survey explains that the electricity consumed by data centers and other computing infrastructure is often generated by thermal power plants, which rely mainly on fossil fuels such as coal and oil. (bharany2022asystematicsurvey chunk 1)

Because these fuels are associated with high CO2 emissions and pollution, thermal power plants contribute to global warming, ozone layer depletion, and premature deaths of living beings. In this framing, the environmental impact of cloud computing is not only due to server-side energy use, but also to the upstream power generation mix supplying that energy. (bharany2022asystematicsurvey chunk 1)

Accordingly, the survey positions energy-efficient and green cloud computing techniques as a response to these harms. By reducing electricity demand in cloud data centers, such techniques lower dependence on fossil-fuel-based thermal generation and thereby reduce associated emissions and environmental damage. (bharany2022asystematicsurvey chunk 1)
